When trying to present a person, an object, an idea, or an event, to give
reasons or an explanation* for something, or to provide steps in doing
something, writers can use an expository essay.
An expository essay is generally divided into three parts—introduction,

is mainly about or the main idea. The body gives supporting details to
explain, to give definitions* and examples, or to provide steps in a process.
The conclusion discusses the main idea again and sometimes finishes with
a call to action.
The basic structure of an expository essay is like the structure of a hamburger.

I’m going to talk about the person I admire most: Mr. Chi Po-lin. I really admire him
because he raised the public’s awareness of the need for environmental protection. At
first, he worked for the government. After he realized that he could offer visual proof of
man-made pollution and damage to the environment, he quit his job, gave up his pension,
and started to make his documentary, Beyond Beauty. In this film, Chi recorded not only
the beautiful landscapes of Taiwan but also the island’s real state. The damaging impact
of human activity that we see is truly shocking and heartbreaking. Chi’s effort has made

importance of courage. By taking great risks to share his stunning views of our homeland
